answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a verifiable-delay entry toll keyed to each agent's public key: before it may trade or vote, an agent must run a strictly sequential computation no parallel hardware can shortcut, slow as a glacier carving rock. One honest agent pays this voyage once and amortizes it over months, but an operator forging a reef of a thousand masks must grind the full delay end to end for every key, since the toll is bound to each identity and cannot be shared. Attacker cost scales linearly per clone, and idle fakes earn nothing.
